More than half of Americans think the Trump administration’s immigration agenda is “too aggressive,” according to a poll carried out three months on from the killings of two American citizens in Minnesota.

Despite the administration’s gear shift on its mass deportation campaign following the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis in January, public opinion is still broadly negative, according to Politico.

In the April poll, 51 percent of Americans said President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign, including the deployment of Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to U.S. cities, is “too aggressive.” A quarter (25 percent) of Americans who voted for Trump in 2024 agreed, according to the poll.

The presence of ICE agents makes cities more dangerous, according to 51 percent of respondents overall. In January, in the midst of the immigration surge in Minnesota, 52 percent felt the same, indicating little change in sentiment.

Among self-identified MAGA voters, 54 percent said they believe Trump's deportation efforts are “about right,” while 28 percent said they were “not aggressive enough.”

open image in gallery More than half of Americans think the Trump administration’s immigration agenda is ‘too aggressive,’ according to a poll, which comes three months on from a federal surge in Minneapolis where two American citizens were killed ( AFP/Getty )

After public outcry over the killings of the U.S. citizens, the Trump administration pivoted its messaging on immigration and overhauled its leadership, with border czar Tom Homan replacing “commander-at-large” Gregory Bovino, while Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem was ousted.

Responding to Politico’s poll, White House spokesperson Abigail Jackson maintained the administration's strategy on immigration was working, touting how Trump was elected to “secure the border and deport criminal illegal aliens” and that he “has done both.”

“The totally secure border means there have been zero releases of illegal aliens for 11 straight months, and the administration remains focused on removing the worst of the worst criminal illegal aliens to secure American communities,” Jackson said. “These commonsense policies are supported by countless Americans.”

The polling comes after an intervention by a group of Trump allies, who have formed a coalition to push his team to resume a more aggressive anti-immigration operation, instead of focusing solely on deporting violent criminals.

The Mass Deportation Coalition, which includes MAGA figures, conservative groups and think tanks close to Trump’s administration, wants to see the president deport all undocumented migrants in the country.

The coalition commissioned polling, conducted by a firm Trump has used in his presidential elections, to back its anti-immigration ideology and said that doubling down on the deportation push will ensure Republicans will win the 2026 midterm elections, Politico reported last month.

open image in gallery The presence of ICE agents makes cities more dangerous, according to 51 percent of respondents overall ( AFP/Getty )

According to the poll carried out by McLaughlin & Associates, 66 percent of likely 2026 voters support the deportation of any migrant who enters the U.S. illegally, and 58 percent said they supported deporting all eligible migrants, not only violent criminals.

Trump voters from the last election were asked whether they supported the president’s goal of exceeding former President Dwight D. Eisenhower’s deportation effort in the 1950s — the largest in U.S. history that saw around one-third of illegal migrants leave the country.

In response, 87 percent said they supported that goal.

The poll also found that 74 percent of Trump voters would be more likely to vote for the Republican candidate for Congress if the president exceeded one million deportations of illegal migrants in 2026.

News.title: Man Utd boost Champions League dreams and leave Chelsea in disarray
News.content:
It is sixth versus third at Stamford Bridge as Chelsea host Manchester United, with the race for the Champions League places hotting up. Manchester United won the reverse fixture 2-1 at Old Trafford back in September, with Chelsea spending most of the game down to 10 men after Robert Sanchez’s fifth-minute red card. If Manchester United were to win tonight, they would complete a league double over Chelsea for just the second time after the 2019/20 campaign. Chelsea have lost just one of their last 12 home league meetings with Manchester United.

Chelsea lost 3-0 at home against Manchester City last weekend. Chelsea have just one Premier league win in their last seven games and go into tonight’s game four points behind Liverpool, who occupy the final Champions League place in fifth.

“That is the great thing about the quality we have in this team,” Liam Rosenior said. “We are capable of a run, but capability is one thing and producing it is another. Time is running out, so we need to be as close to perfect as possible in every aspect of the game. If we do that, we have the potential to win every game for the rest of the season.

“When the team was its best with players like John [Terry], Frank [Lampard], Didier [Drogba], it was a team of big personalities fighting for the shirt, not a team of egos. I feel we have those kinds of characters in our squad, and that is what we need to show in this moment.”

Enzo Fernandez has been suspended for their last two games but is back available for selection tonight, although it remains to be seen in what capacity.

Manchester United lost 2-1 at home to Leeds last Monday but remain in third, level on points with Aston Villa, three points ahead of Liverpool and seven ahead of Chelsea.

“It is an important game,” Michael Carrick said. “We are in a good position in the league and we want to keep building on that. It is a tough place to go, always has been. We have had some tough games down there. Most of the time they have been good games in terms of what it brings. It has the feelings of a real, proper game so we will be ready for that. We have prepared well and take the confidence from what we have built. We did not get the result we wanted against Leeds but the character that we showed we have to take into this game with an extra player and make the most of it.”

Manchester United will be without centre-backs Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez for the trip to Stamford Bridge due to suspension. Maguire was given an extra game ban for improper conduct following his red card against Bournemouth whilst Martinez was sent off against Leeds. They could have a real centre-back problem tonight with Matthijs de Ligt still out injured and Leny Yoro set to miss out. Kobbie Mainoo though could be fit to return having missed the loss to Leeds.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Crying shame as Tottenham hearts are broken by Brighton
News.content:
I’m sorry for the result, for the players because they are suffering too much. Today we deserved to win the game against a great Brighton. Congratulations for the level of players and everything [but] especially in that moment of the game we could not concede that goal to Georginio Rutter.

I am positive and I am proud of my players because they played a fantastic game with character and spirit, what I asked of them. To deserve to play in this stadium for this club we have to be stronger than this result, to prepare for the next game against Wolverhampton to win the game. If you are strong like today, I think we can compete again.

I said we have to be stronger, to follow me again because I want to help them. I want [them to realise they can] change the mentality because the mentality is the most important part.

Now it is too easy to get down. Now we have to work and find the conditions to win again. Because I am coach of Tottenham I know my players, I know their qualities. I know my players as people now.

I know we are fighting to keep in the Premier League. It’s a very difficult moment but we are lucky, every one of us, to work in this club, for these fans, with this incredible atmosphere today. You could feel the atmosphere was like we were qualifying for the Champions League not against relegation. Until the end we’re going to fight every game, give our best and if we give our best I think it is not the end.

Today I watched the signs, the blood, the quality, character, organisation with and without the ball. [We have] the right spirit we need to reach our target and fight until the end of the season.

We have to improve in a lot of things [technically and tactically] but it’s not the crucial part. The crucial part is to keep this mentality. I told them to come on Monday morning with the same behaviour they showed today. I don’t want to work with sad people, negative people. I accepted to come to Tottenham because I am positive we can stay in the Premier league next season, one hundred per cent.

News.title: ‘World-class’ Hannah Hampton saves Lionesses in Iceland
News.content:
Hannah Hampton had been a spectator for much of the first half against Iceland; the odd touch here and there, a pass to one of her defenders every so often. England had dominated possession and looked on course for a comfortable victory after Alessia Russo put them ahead in the 21st minute.

How quickly a game of football can change. Iceland were superior in the second period and would have equalised had it not been for Hampton’s heroics. The goalkeeper made three superb saves in the final 15 minutes to ensure England held on to their slender lead and maintained a 100 per cent record in World Cup qualifying.

Sarina Wiegman described Hampton as “world class” afterwards while Russo added: “Big moments kept us in it and she showed up three or four times to keep us in it and get us the three points. Sometimes you need someone to step up like that.”

News.title: More Red Lion than Three Lions as YouTubers put on 20-goal show
News.content:
One might say, not bad money for mucking about on the internet, but perhaps the fairer comparison is to say simply that these are gifted and hardworking entertainers who are using the technologies of their time to meet their punters where they are. The closest analogue to this Sidemen charity event would be Soccer Aid, and who could say with conviction that Angry Ginge is any more or less deserving of fame and fortune than, say, Olly Murs or Lee Mack (seven Soccer Aid caps each), let alone that bloke whose sole meal ticket was being Robbie Williams’ mate?

At the astonishingly decrepit age of 50, your correspondent must have been pretty much the oldest person in the place on Saturday, with the exception of the dutiful mums and dads bringing excited, starstruck teenagers for a family day out. Wembley said that the tickets, priced between £15 and £35, sold out in 2½ hours. The only downside would be that the bar takings would be a tiny fraction of an England game. But maybe that makes for a more pleasant Tube ride home anyway.

On the subject of money, even if they weren’t doing very nicely out of content creation, one would not advise any of the Sidemen to give up the day job and give football a go. The level was that of a reasonable pub team, although one or two did stand out. Angry Ginge, who recently got up the nose of Roy Keane (hardly alone in that), scored the opener with a thumping, Harry Maguire-ish header. TBJZL (real name: Tobi Brown) scored a genuinely delightful free kick with the outside of his boot. The teams were evenly matched and generally got on with the game with no more or less prima donna behaviour than we see each weekend in the Premier League. Mark Clattenburg, that old ham, was the referee and got involved wherever possible, including when he booked Max Fosh, only to have the yellow card stolen from him by the conjuror and set on fire.

News.title: Red Roses make light of absentees to crush Scotland with power game
News.content:
A record-breaking party for Scottish sport, and England’s Red Roses spoilt it.

On the day of the largest standalone crowd for a women’s sporting fixture north of the border, England’s march towards an eighth successive Six Nations title continued with aplomb, as the world champions delivered a 12-try clinic at Murrayfield.

England were depleted but one might not have known, inflicting Scotland’s heaviest defeat in this fixture since 2011. In hindsight, and considering the extraordinary depth at John Mitchell’s disposal, it seems bonkers to bleat about an availability crisis but the truth is that no other side – women’s or men’s – in the world could manage England’s absentee list and maintain such dominance. Never mind England’s second team, their thirds would have a good shot at winning the Women’s Six Nations right now.

Three second rows – Zoe Stratford, Abbie Ward and Rosie Galligan – are pregnant, as is hooker Lark Atkin-Davies, while five others have suffered championship-ending injuries. Seven of the 13 forwards who played in last autumn’s World Cup final win were absent, including Alex Matthews, who is only a short-term loss, and England were down to what could be considered as a third-choice lock pairing and a debutant, Demelza Short, at blindside while Ellie Kildunne, one of the Red Roses’ superstars, started on the wing for the first time in white.

It made no difference. After a nervy start against a Scotland side bulwarked by record home support – there were 30,498 packed into Murrayfield, beating the near-19,000 who witnessed Scotland’s footballers defeat Jamaica at Hampden in 2019 – England ran riot. Zoe Harrison was immaculate both out of hand and with the boot (she was successful with each of her 12 conversions), underlining her status as the world’s best women’s fly-half. Outside of Harrison, both Emma Sing and Kildunne provided cutting edge, while Meg Jones, the captain, gave the visitors direction and momentum in the midfield.

News.title: Iran tells Trump: Our uranium is not going anywhere
News.content:
Donald Trump is elated. He appears to have just secured the breakthrough his administration has pursued so doggedly. “THANK YOU!” he exclaimed, noting on Truth Social that “THE STRAIT OF IRAN IS FULLY OPEN AND READY FOR FULL PASSAGE”.

It is possible that Tehran – which won’t mind the Strait of Hormuz being called the Strait of Iran one bit – is making a significant concession. There does seem to be genuine optimism in certain quarters about the progress of negotiations. The Lebanese ceasefire is something Iran had been demanding, so a reciprocal step of some kind would be logical.

Yet it would be wise to inject a note of caution, for the moment at least. The announcement was made on X by Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s foreign minister, but the wording of his post was strikingly similar to one he published on 8 April when the ceasefire was first agreed.

“The passage for all commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz is declared completely open for the remaining period of the ceasefire,” he wrote. On 8 April, he said: “Iran… declares the Strait of Hormuz open for all commercial shipping for the duration of the agreed two-week period.”

A more ominous comparison can be drawn from the closing lines of each post. Both suggest that Iran’s definition of the word “open” may differ from Washington’s. Today’s post signalled that ships would be allowed to transit along “the coordinated route as already announced by [the] Ports and Maritime Organisation of the Islamic Rep. of Iran”. The 8 April post warned that “transit must strictly follow the coordinated route as already announced by the Ports and Maritime Organisation of the Islamic Rep. of Iran”.

This may explain why Mr Trump swiftly tempered his gratitude by declining to lift his counter-blockade. The US president will interpret Mr Araghchi’s post as a sign that his pressure on Iran – and its faltering economy – is beginning to tell. That is possible. Iran, however, may conclude it has proved a point: that it can close the strait whenever it chooses, and that, for now, reopening it suits Tehran. Or it could mean very little, and that little has actually changed.

The markets are taking the more optimistic view. Oil fell below $90 a barrel, its lowest level in nearly six weeks, within minutes of Mr Araghchi’s post. Perhaps that optimism is warranted – but not everyone will be convinced just yet.

News.title: Vaccinating pregnant women against RSV significantly reduces infant hospitalisations, says study
News.content:
Vaccinating expectant mothers against RSV reduces hospital admissions in young infants by at least 80 per cent, according to a major study of nearly 300,000 babies in England.

The research – the largest real world analysis of maternal RSV vaccinations – tracked the electronic health records of 289,399 infants born in England in the year after September 2024, when the rollout of RSV shots for pregnant women began.

Researchers compared the rates of RSV-related hospitalisations among babies whose mothers did and did not receive an immunisation. Overall, they found that vaccinating expectant mothers at least two weeks before childbirth reduced the risk of hospitalisation by 81.3 per cent.

Timing mattered: if the vaccine was administered four weeks ahead of birth protection rose to 85 per cent, as there is more time to boost the immune system and pass antibodies to the baby through the placenta. If the shot was administered 10 days before childbirth, protection dropped to 55 per cent – any sooner and the effect was negligible.

“We’re able to say it’s definitively really good protection against hospitalisation, against being so sick that you need to be admitted for things like oxygen and feeding support,” said Dr Conall Watson, a consultant epidemiologist at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and national programme lead for RSV.

“The size of the analysis also means that we have been able to confirm strong protection in preterm infants, as long as there is a two week gap between vaccination and birth,” he told the Telegraph, adding that the study is 40 times bigger than previous clinical trials.

RSV, or respiratory syncytial virus, is a common virus that can cause severe respiratory illness, including bronchiolitis and pneumonia, especially in infants and young children.

According to the World Health Organization, 3.6 million children under five are hospitalised every year because of RSV, while 100,000 die. The vast majority of these fatalities are in low and middle income countries, where access to intensive care is more limited.

Dr Watson said the results of the UKHSA study present a “huge opportunity” to prevent death in these countries, by stopping hospitalisations from happening in the first place.

In England, maternal RSV vaccine uptake is rising – from 55 per cent during the study period, to 64.1 per cent in November 2025. Dr Watson said the latest results should “give great reassurance to pregnant women that vaccination is absolutely the right thing to do to protect their baby”.

The study was presented on Saturday at the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases. Researchers said they hope to next assess how protection changes later in infancy.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s ‘give it to Bruno Fernandes’ tactic pays off as Carrick’s men breeze past Chelsea despite defensive crisis
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES was getting animated on the touchline one minute and was animated in celebration the next.

Fernandes had a lengthy discussion with Michael Carrick during the stoppage for Wesley Fofana’s treatment.





He was then on Benjamin Sesko’s case, advising the Manchester United striker on his positioning and runs.

As soon as the game resumed, Fernandes held off the flaky Alejandro Garnacho to cut back for Matheus Cunha to clip in.

United staff were on their feet in the dugout and a few fans in the hospitality rows behind them soon broke cover.

‘If in doubt, give it to Fernandes’ is a tried-and-tested tactic for United and it still has merit.

Fernandes was the last player off the pitch as he conducted a post-match interview to the soundtrack of his song being belted out by United fans.

Inevitably, Fernandes was also handed the man of the match cylinder.

Up until Cunha’s breakthrough, United’s front four was too individualistic and detached. Fernandes provided the glue to bring them together.

Sesko played an underrated role in the goal, occupying Moises Caicedo as the ball bounced onto Cunha’s right boot on an otherwise unmemorable night for the Slovenian.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Fernandes has reined in his whingeing and usually opts for constructive criticism these days.

Carrick did most of the talking during their chat and it is rare to see Fernandes not doing the talking. Whatever they discussed worked.

Cunha has a similar edge to Fernandes and channelled him as he headed towards the tunnel, questioning referee Michael Oliver on his earlier booking.

The Brazilian could have basked in the glory of his eighth United goal yet did not want to blunt that edge. He was not particularly sharp on the ball until he scored.



But Cunha’s character has lifted this United side. He was bullish when replaced by Mason Mount and celebrated wildly with Casemiro by the tunnel at full-time.

United’s away-dayers tend to be at their loudest at Chelsea and their raucous following contrasted with the apathy of the hosts.

Carrick was in the dugout alongside Ole Gunnar Solskjaer for United’s only three wins in their previous 17 matches at Stamford Bridge.

United have won seven times at Chelsea this century and Carrick has been involved in six: two as a player, three as first-team coach and now as head coach.

Back at the scene of his first Premier League match in management in 2021, this was another feather in Carrick’s cap.



United have dropped 17 points against the bottom six yet taken 18 points against the top six. Four of those six wins have come under Carrick.

The ramifications of United’s tepid defeat to Leeds were minimal and that blemish now looks forgivable.

The manner of a first win at Chelsea in six years will be especially pleasing given the decimated state of United’s central defence, compounded by a hip injury that Leny Yoro sustained in training.



Carrick had innumerable auxiliary options and some United supporters advocated the return of a back three.

Moving Noussair Mazraoui inside to centre back next to the raw Ayden Heaven was logical.

They were bookended by the squad’s two-longest serving members in Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw so, even with five defenders out, United had some stability and kept a clean sheet.

They rode their luck, as they did in some of Solskjaer’s big away wins. This felt like a homage from Carrick to his Norwegian friend.

It was not a vintage United victory but at this stage of the season results take precedence.



Despite the Saturday evening kick-off time, it did not feel like a marquee match between two Champions League qualification competitors.

It was a bloodless match even as United fans bayed for Garnacho’s blood.

The former United man had a brief jog in front of the away section in the Shed End, which will have warmed him up more than the exercise.



Carrick quickly touched base with Jonathan Woodgate and United looked like they were considering a defensive rejig in response to Garnacho’s early arrival.

Garnacho fluffed his first touch to cheers from the United fans and then switched with Pedro Neto.

The Argentine was dispossessed right in front of the United fans by Diogo Dalot. Mazraoui, Casemiro and Bryan Mbeumo all heartily clapped Dalot and the Garnacho chant soon restarted.

United players took it in turns to introduce Garnacho to the turf throughout the night.

He then started picking out a red shirt so often Chelsea fans might have questioned his allegiance.

Sports.title: ‘Gone too far’ – Tony Adams calls for rule change to be introduced that could hurt Arsenal
Sports.content:
GUNNERS legend Tony Adams is calling for a crackdown on grappling at set-pieces.

Adams accepts such methods were used in his era — but argues they have “gone too far” today.





The ex-centre-back’s old club Arsenal lead the way in maximising dead balls.

But the former Gunners captain said: “The levels of set-pieces — and the contacts and blocks — it’s just gone too far.

“I was talking the other day about 1993 when ‘the donkey won the derby’ [in the FA Cup semi-final].

“Andy Linighan runs to block Spurs’ Neil Ruddock and I go around the back — free, bang, in you go.



“I’ve scored the header and in the FA Cup final, I’ve blocked for Andy and he got the winner against Sheffield Wednesday.

“Viv Anderson taught me how to do it when he came from Forest.

“He used to take people out. We had a competition in the ’89 season. He got five. I think I got six. We blocked for each other.

“But now, if you’re teaching defenders how to defend from corners… it used to be ball, player.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Now it’s just about grabbing hold of you.”

Arsenal head to City today desperately requiring a victory to get their title charge back on track.

The Full Arsenal on YouTube SunSport have launched a dedicated Arsenal channel on YouTube! The Full Arsenal Podcast is your home for everything about the Gunners. From match reactions and tactical breakdowns to transfer talk, match previews, tactical analysis and honest fan debate… The Full Arsenal covers it all. Subscribe to The Full Arsenal here

Mikel Arteta needs his big players to step up and Adams has spoken glowingly about Declan Rice.

Adams called for Rice to be made captain at the start of this season — not Martin Odegaard.

The Gunners icon felt the team, missing injured Odegaard, lacked leadership in their 2-0 Carabao Cup final loss to City.



Adams added: “You’re looking at Bernardo Silva with his relationship with Pep [Guardiola].

“You could just see that chemistry there and a leader. I didn’t see the same with Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Wesley Fofana and Marc Cucurella struggle in dismal Man Utd defeat but Liam Delap keeps fighting
Sports.content:
AND THAT, is why fans at Stamford Bridge are so unhappy…

Chelsea were forced into an early change when Estevao hobbled straight down the tunnel after 15 minutes with what could only be a muscle injury.





The Blues were largely dominant in the first half at home, with Enzo Fernandez coming close, and even got the ball in the back of the net via Liam Delap, only to see the offside flag raised against Cole Palmer.

Again, though, for all their dominance, they were caught out and conceded before being booed off at half-time – this time it was Matheus Cunha who struck into the top corner.



Chelsea were chasing the game in the second half, and rattled the crossbar twice to no avail after crosses into the box from the right-hand side.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the Blues…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 5

It would feel harsh to blame him for the opener. Truthfully, it was a great strike that he couldn’t get near.

With the ball at his feet, he was pretty good and managed things well, while saving what he needed to in the second half.



MALO GUSTO – 4

Gusto has been largely hit and miss for Chelsea this season, but this was a miss.

He wasn’t massively tested by Cunha defensively on the Man Utd left, but going forward, his deliveries into the box weren’t up to the standard of the missing Reece James.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

WESLEY FOFANA – 3

Aerial prowess and physicality are two things Chelsea need from a centre-back signing in the summer.

But for now, they have Wesley Fofana attempting to provide it.

Those two things are hardly more needed as a defender than when you face man mountain Benjamin Sesko.



The Frenchman had hobbled off the pitch holding his rib when United scored their opener – and some will say he should’ve been man enough to play on, which he did so after the goal went in.

JORREL HATO – 6

For my money, Jorrel Hato is one of the most promising young defenders in the Premier League, and starting against Man Utd at 19 is no mean feat.

He was good on the ball and strong in the tackle, showing great recovery speed too.

The only criticism of him is that he perhaps wasn’t involved in as many defensive actions as Fofana next to him. Physically he is still lacking a little.



MARC CUCURELLA – 3

It was Cucurella’s header from a Reece James cross that won Chelsea this fixture last season, and today it felt like watching Marcos Alonso back in blue at Stamford Bridge.

He was good going forward, but caught out at the back, with the Spaniard too high up and the wrong side of Bruno Fernandes, who delivered another assist for Cunha’s opener.

MOISES CAICEDO – 6

Caicedo was given a special welcome ahead of kick-off after signing a contract extension at Stamford Bridge in the week. But for a while, he hasn’t looked like the same player who was being called the best in the world in his position earlier this season.

This was a reminder of how good he can be, winning everything in midfield and spraying balls forward at will.



Unfortunately, he was let down by the defence behind him.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 5

Fernandez was finally allowed out of the naughty corner for flirting with a move to Real Madrid, and returned to the starting XI, though NOT in his usual role as captain.

He played like he was trying to prove a point, too, coming close with a curling effort that fell just wide of the post after nutmegging a United defender.

Enzo looked a threat, and combined well with his teammates, but wasn’t able to provide the kind of moment that could really drag his side back into the game.



ESTEVAO – 6

Looked a real danger early on, and came close with a low curling effort from the right-wing.

He was given a standing ovation as he hobbled off injured, though, and went straight down the tunnel after 15 minutes.

COLE PALMER – 5

Palmer will feel hard done by that he didn’t win his side a penalty early on, with Man Utd fans chanting ‘City reject’ at him while he was on the floor.

He showed flashes of the Palmer that Chelsea fans have grown to adore, but not enough moments of real creativity, and not enough of the sharpshooting he is revered for.

It was his opposite number, Bruno Fernandes, who won the battle of the number 10’s.



PEDRO NETO – 4

Neto was left completely and utterly frustrated tonight. Frustrated by himself, frustrated by the woodwork, and frustrated by others.

His touch wasn’t good enough more often than not, neither was his passing – and on the rare occasion he did put in a really dangerous delivery, it rattled back off the crossbar.

LIAM DELAP – 6

With Joao Pedro injured, Delap was called upon to be the starting number nine despite scoring just one Premier League goal all season.

He thought he had doubled that tally just before half-time with a tap into an empty net, only for it to be ruled out by the offside flag raised against Palmer.

Delap came close again in the second half, rattling the crossbar with a headed effort that riled up the home fans, but was ultimately left frustrated at Stamford Bridge.



SUBS:

ALEJANDRO GARNACHO (ESTEVAO, 15) –

It was a really rough night for the Argentine winger.

He was brought on earlier than planned due to Estevao’s injury, and United fans were unrelenting in their chanting towards him, jeering every poor touch or tackle on him.

If there were any truth in social media rumours that he misses Man Utd, they certainly don’t miss him, and wouldn’t take him back after today’s showing.

TREVOH CHALOBAH (WESLEY FOFANA, 81) – 5

Didn’t have much time to impact the game as Chelsea pushed for a winner.

Didn’t have much time to impact the game as Chelsea pushed for a winner.

Didn’t have much time to impact the game.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Mazraoui impresses in EIGHTH different position as Sesko struggles in individualistic front four
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED skirted past Chelsea at Stamford Bridge thanks to a lone Matheus Cunha finish.

Defences were on top in the cagey affair in West London, but the visitors came out on top to defend their position as the best of the rest behind the title challengers.



Several stars stood out for the Red Devils, especially in the back line.



But the result does not mean there were not those who failed to turn in convincing performances.

Here’s how SunSport United reporter Samuel Luckhurst rated the players’ performance…

Fumbled an Enzo Fernandez shot that he should have held onto but Liam Delap‘s conversion on the rebound was offside.

Indecisive a couple of times but it did not cost him.

Returned to the starting XI after illness contributed to his bench berth against Leeds.

Endeared himself to United fans by dispossessing Alejandro Garnacho and made his experience count.

Occupied his eighth different role for United at centre back in a two to complement the left-footed Ayden Heaven and his reading of the game was impressive.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS



Was more than up for the fight with Liam Delap, having squared up to him last year.

Ayden Heaven – 6

Had some hairy moments on his first start since January. Committed two fouls outside the area and one led to a free kick.

Executed the odd sliding tackle that would have buoyed him.

Stayed at left back, despite playing at centre back in a back four, and had a steady first half.



Did little attacking but was never going to with United’s defence depleted and he was a reassuring presence.

Chelsea played the ball through United’s midfield with such ease you had to wonder whether Erik ten Hag was back in charge.

Casemiro was not as commanding against the dynamic duo of Moises Caicedo and Fernandez. Still left Garnacho on the turf with a clean tackle.

Botched a promising breakaway.

Lacked the control he has recently exerted in games until a stoppage allowed him to chat with Carrick.

The next time Fernandes got the ball, he assisted Matheus Cunha to make it 1-0.



Matheus Cunha – 7

Had little of the ball and it showed when he tackled a first touch from Mbeumo’s lay-off to get booked.

Made amends with a cleanly clipped opening goal.

United did not play to his strengths and the front four were too individualistic.



Had an underrated role in Cunha’s goal as he occupied Caicedo when the ball bounced across but had a night to forget.

Sports.title: Forgotten England star, 30, bags over £100,000 per GAME in image rights despite struggling in Championship
Sports.content:
FORGOTTEN Man City and England star Kalvin Phillips has banked a whopping £5million in his image rights firm over the last four seasons – despite only playing 46 games in that time.

That is the equivalent to more than £100,000 per game in off-pitch earnings, in addition to his £150,000-a-week wages he picks up from City.





Phillips, a 31-cap England international, has signed lucrative sponsorship deals with the likes of Adidas.

Fresh accounts for the forgotten midfielder’s image rights firm, KP23 Ltd, show he is earning £1.3million a year in off the pitch earnings.

Despite his international experience, Phillips is not in England boss Thomas Tuchel’s thoughts ahead of the World Cup in the summer.

He has only played once for Pep Guardiola‘s side this season, a seven-minute cameo in the League Cup third round against Huddersfield.



He completed a shock loan transfer to Championship club Sheffield United in February to get him back playing regular football again.

But he has played just three times after missing games through injury and suspension.

City are understood to be continuing to cover the majority of his reported wages.

The 30-year-old signed for Man City from Leeds United on a six-year deal in 2022 in a £42million deal, rising to £45m with add-ons.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Before his loan to Bramall Lane, the midfielder has previously had two more temporary moves away from Man City.

In January 2024, he joined West Ham on a six-month deal but was limited to just 10 appearances.

Phillips failed to make a positive impression in East London as he was sent off in a 2-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest and at fault for a penalty in a 4-3 loss at Newcastle.

Ipswich Town took a punt on Phillips during their season in the Premier League in which he played 22 times.

However, he could not help the Tractor Boys stay in the division as they were relegated back to the Championship.



Despite his limited action with the Blades, manager Chris Wilder has insisted he would be welcomed back in the summer.

He said: “He’ll have a lot of people still after him.

“We’ve brought a really good pro in. He was unlucky with his injury and he’s not played as much as he wanted to play.

“I spoke to him and said we’d love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club if that is a possibility.

“He certainly ticks the box in terms of personality and characteristics, off the pitch and on it.

“If there’s an opportunity I’m sure we’ll try and explore that one.”

Sports.title: Chelsea 0 Man Utd 1: Cunha puts huge dent in Blues’ Champions League hopes as Garnacho suffers horror United reunion
Sports.content:
BRUNO Fernandes is closing in on a personal milestone.

But more significantly, another crucial contribution from the Manchester United skipper helped his club take another big step towards the Champions League.



And perhaps edged Michael Carrick closer to being given the manager’s job permanently.



Fernandes’ cross for Matheus Cunha to score the only goal, completely against the run of play, was his 18th Premier League assist of the season.

He has five games left to match or better the record of 20 held by Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry.

While Fernandes was United’s captain fantastic again, the man who shares his name found himself stripped of his power.

Enzo Fernandez was back in the Chelsea team after a two-game internal ban for talking out of turn and encouraging speculation linking him to Real Madrid.

But having been vice-captain all season, Fernandez lost the armband to Moises Caicedo after his fellow £100m midfielder extended his own Blues contract last week.

To be fair to Fernandez, he and his team did everything but score, hitting the bar twice as well as the post once and deserved at least a point.

The cold, hard truth, though, is that Liam Rosenior’s team have not found the net in the league for more than four games and nearly six and a half hours.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Time is running out on their bid to finish in the top five, and possibly on Rosenior’s tenure as head coach.



Nearly 15 minutes before the end, the home fans were already singing “We want our Chelsea back” and abusing Stamford Bridge supremo Behdad Eghbali.

In a pre-match interview, Cole Palmer reaffirmed his commitment to winning big trophies with the Blues with one breath.

With the next he admitted the reality that “everything changes” if the Blues do not qualify for the Champions League.

The latest revelations about the elaborate, high-risk, loss-making financial structure under the current owners suggest Chelsea need to be back for good in Europe’s most lucrative competition.



Unless Rosenior can relight the fire of Palmer and the rest of the team, they will be in the Europa League or worse next season.

And in that scenario, Rosenior may well not be in charge anymore.

United, with four centre backs injured, will have been grateful to learn Chelsea top scorer Joao Pedro was out with a thigh problem.

But the Blues still made the better start.



After Estevao had tickled the far post with a left-foot shot, the Brazilian winger pulled up with what looked like a hamstring problem, and on came Alejandro Garnacho.

But not before the former United man had to warm up in front of the away fans who increased the volume of the abusive chant they had already been singing.

United themselves gave the travelling hordes nothing to get excited about until the 25th minute when Bruno Fernandes played in Bryan Mbeumo down the right.

From the resulting cross, Cunha could have shot instantly. Instead a heavy touch led to him fouling Jorrel Hato and earning a yellow card.



Man Utd ratings vs Chelsea MAN UTD showed their Champions League credentials with a composed victory at Chelsea. The Red Devils kept the Blues at arm’s length despite having just one fit centre-back Full-back Noussair Mazraoui was forced to fill in in the middle alongside 19-year-old Ayden Heaven. Matheus Cunha put the Red Devils ahead just before half time and though the Blues did strike the woodwork, it never felt like an equaliser was inevitable. Captain Bruno Fernandes brushed his former team-mate Garnacho aside to deliver the killer pass for the Brazilian. And the result means United have an unassailable-looking ten-point gap to the Blues in sixth, with five Champions League places on offer. Here’s how SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst rated the Man Utd stars.

But the home side remained on top. Fernandez did the hard work by half-nutmegging, half-outmuscling Noussair Mazraoui, only to curl his shot wide.

The Argentinian did force Senne Lammens into his first save, but Palmer was offside from the rebound before teeing up Delap.

Then a dangerous Pedro Neto cross eluded the Chelsea centre forward and hit Fernandez.

But when your luck’s out, it is really out.



While Wes Fofana was off the pitch injured, Fernandes held off Marc Cucurella and Garnacho to reach the byline before crossing into the area where the Chelsea defender would have been.

This time Cunha did hit it first time and somehow it was 1-0.

The half-time boos from the home fans were hardly deserved.

The game resumed in a flat atmosphere.



Chelsea ratings vs Man Utd CHELSEA hit a new low as Liam Rosenior’s men made it four Premier League defeats in a row without scoring. Despite Man Utd having just one fit centre-back in 19-year-old Ayden Heaven, the Blues hardly looked like battering the door down. Liam Rosenior may point to hitting the woodwork three times as proof they deserved something from the game, but Michael Carrick will still be delighted with how his threadbare back line handled Chelsea’s threat. The Blues suffered a huge blow with Estevao going off injured early in the first half. And ex-Man Utd ace Alejandro Garnacho didn’t play like a man with a point to prove to his old club when he came on as a replacement. The winger constantly gave the ball away and was partly responsible for the goal when Bruno Fernandes breezed past him to find Matheus Cunha for the only goal of the game. Here’s how SunSport’s Lloyd Canfield rated the Blues stars after a performance that won’t live long in the memory.

Fernandes clipped a left-foot shot wide from the edge of the box.

The home support woke up when Delap met Neto’s cross and his header came back off the bar with Lammens beaten.

The game was opening up a little, and when United broke, a deflection on Fernandes’ shot had Sanchez scrambling to keep it out.

At the other end, there was more agony when another great delivery by Neto was headed against the underside of the crossbar by Fofana.



Chances dried up, and things began to turn toxic for Chelsea.

Carrick sent on Mason Mount, who set up Kai Havertz for the goal which won Chelsea the Champions League less than five years ago.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The booing of Mount almost turned to cheers, but Caicedo’s long-range drive whistled just wide.

Fernandes and one young English manager marched on. Fernandez and another stumbled, again.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho ‘lined up for sensational return to Real Madrid’ with ex-Chelsea and Man Utd boss ‘high on shortlist’
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has been linked with a sensational return to Real Madrid.

The legendary Portuguese boss is currently chasing top-flight glory with Benfica, having been knocked out of the Champions League by Los Blancos in the round of 16.



But according to reports from Record, he is now being eyed up as a replacement for Alvaro Arbeloa.



The interest comes as club president Florentino Perez and Co consider their options in the wake of their Champions League exit at the hands of Bayern Munich last week.

The loss coincided with a drop in league form, with the side taking just a point from their last two league clashes against Mallorca and Girona.

The dropped points mean they now sit nine points adrift of rivals Barcelona at the summit, and alarm bells are being rung regarding Arbeloa’s long-term future at the club.

Mourinho has reportedly been placed high on a shortlist of potential replacements, should the former academy coach be ousted from his post.



The 63-year-old former Manchester United tactician is said to be open to a return, despite tensions flaring during his departure in 2013.

The Special One previously spent a three-year spell in the Santiago Bernabeu dugout between 2010-2013.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta's stirring final message to Arsenal stars before Man City showdown
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta's stirring final message to Arsenal stars before Man City showdown

Arsenal head to the Etihad on Sunday afternoon, knowing a win over Manchester City would see them put one hand on their first Premier League title for 23 years

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal side can take a huge step towards the title by beating Man City (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has delivered a rabble-rousing message to his Arsenal players ahead of their title decider at Manchester City.

‌



Arteta told them to “go for it” as they look to deliver a performance against their biggest rivals which will blow away any lingering doubts.

‌



The Gunners are still six points ahead but City have a game in hand and if Pep Guardiola ’s men win on Sunday and beat Burnley three days later they can knock Arsenal off the top on goal difference.

‌



It will be a huge test of Arsenal’s mentality and determination to win the title having been on top of the Premier League for nearly 200 days.

But Arteta delivered a strong speech and says his final message before they go out onto the pitch will be to tell his stars to believe in themselves.

Mikel Arteta lights FIRE at Arsenal training in bid to get Gunners back on track READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal need to make a statement vs Man City to avoid fresh heartbreak READ MORE :

Gunners boss Arteta said: “Go for it. Let’s be ourselves and go for it, put everything we have on that pitch. Huge belief, huge conviction and go for it because we are more than capable of doing it.”

‌



City boss Guardiola has insisted that if his side lose then the title will be all over and Arsenal will be crowned champions.

However, Arsenal have been wobbling as they lost their last Premier League game to Bournemouth, they lost to City in the Carabao Cup final and also crashed out of the FA Cup.

The Gunners are into the Champions League semi final but they are under the spotlight because if they blow the title from here then it would be a devastating blow for Arteta.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal's defeat to Bournemouth has opened the door for Man City in the title race

But rather than fear the pressure, Arteta urged his players to embrace it and use it in a positive way.

Arteta added: “One hundred per cent. We are exactly where we want to be and there have been a lot of positive things and I don’t see anything that has to hold you back.

Article continues below

“We are where we want to be in the period where you want to be playing against an opponent that requires the best out of you so it doesn’t get much better than that.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta makes telling comment about his relationship with Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta makes telling comment about his relationship with Pep Guardiola

Mikel Arteta and Pep Guardiola worked alongside one another at Manchester City but have now gone from colleagues to title rivals since the former's move to Arsenal

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola and Mikel Arteta are competing for the Premier League title (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The cold war between the Premier League’s fiercest managerial rivals finally appears to have thawed. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta made it clear that he has not spoken to Pep Guardiola since they met in the Carabao Cup final last month.

‌



But even after Manchester City ’s win at Wembley, tension has been replaced by respect ahead of Sunday’s title decider at the Etihad.

‌



Arteta famously worked under City boss Guardiola and learned from the best before taking up his current job as Arsenal manager in December 2019.

‌



City were not happy with the nature of Arteta’s departure but the pair remained close until their relationship really hit a low after Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad in September 2024.

Accusations flew that day after Arsenal had Leandro Trossard was sent off, City midfielder Rodri suffered a serious knee injury and Erling Haaland delivered his “stay humble” taunts.

Mikel Arteta's stirring final message to Arsenal stars before Man City showdown READ MORE :

City accused Arsenal of time-wasting while Guardiola was furious amid the back-and-forth when Arteta claimed he had “all the information” about his former club. The feud was developing into Fergie v Wenger and actually only heightened the tension in the title race.

‌



They have gone toe-to-toe in title races and it is back to that point again with this season on the line in the latest instalment of Guardiola v Arteta.

The first hint of a thaw came after City won at Chelsea last Sunday when Guardiola insisted Arsenal deserved “respect” for what they had done this season. It was over and above the usual pre-match niceties.

View 2 Images The two became close during their time working together at Manchester City (Image: OLI SCARFF/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



But Arteta insisted their friendship - which dates back nearly 30 years to the Barcelona academy days - is back on track and actually they would connect instantly again over coffee or dinner.

Arteta added: “I think in a relationship, first of all it is the distance. When you spend 14 hours a day together as we did and when you don’t spend any, there is a big difference.

“And then obviously you look at where we are, we are both challenging for very similar things, so that changes the relationship but that does not change, for sure, the way I feel about him and the times we had together.

‌



“But if I have lunch with him or a coffee in two minutes that relationship comes back to nature because we are very capable of separating things as a professional rivalry and the personal relationship and that will stay the same.”

That partnership and rivalry has been intense. It has shaped the title race in three of the past four seasons. They have got too much at stake on Sunday to be anything but enemies. But respect and cordial relations have been restored. Until at least things kick off at the Etihad.

Sports.title: Man Utd edge out toothless Chelsea in major Champions League boost - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Man Utd edge out toothless Chelsea in major Champions League boost - 5 talking points

CHELSEA 0-1 MAN UTD: A strike from Matheus Cunha was all that separated the sides at Stamford Bridge in a game which had significant implications in the race for Champions League football

View 4 Images Matheus Cunha's goal was enough for Manchester United (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Manchester United have taken a massive step towards securing Champions League football after their hard-fought 1-0 win against Chelsea. The Red Devils claimed all three points at Stamford Bridge courtesy of Matheus Cunha's first-half goal.

‌



It was nervy for Michael Carrick's side, who had to fend off wave after wave of Chelsea attack, as the hosts searched for a response to ease the rising pressure on Liam Rosenior. But United held on to strengthen their grip on third place.

‌



Carrick's men came into the clash dealing with a crisis in defence, but ended up coming away with their first clean sheet in nearly two months. Chelsea, meanwhile, couldn't find their shooting boots and have now lost their last four Premier League games.

‌



Here are five talking points from Stamford Bridge.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Michael Carrick leaves door open for Marcus Rashford return amid Man Utd transfer dilemma READ MORE :

1. Mazraoui the makeshift

Crisis? What crisis? Noussair Mazraoui was deployed as a makeshift centre-back by Carrick, who faced a crisis in defence pre-match. Four central defenders were missing after Leny Yoro picked up an injury in training and joined Matthijs de Ligt, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez on the sidelines.

‌



But Mazraoui performed admirably next to 19-year-old Ayden Heaven in a position he'd never played before at United. It's another strong to the Moroccan's bow and his versatility could be key to his long-term future with the Red Devils.

View 4 Images Noussair Mazraoui did well as a central defender (Image: Chelsea Football Club/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

3. Estevao's early bath

Regarded as one of the sport's most talented teenagers, it feels like we're yet to see the best of Estevao on a consistent basis. And we'll have to wait even longer after the 18-year-old came off injured.

‌



Probing at United's defence inside opening quarter of an hour, Estevao burst into the box and fired a scuffed attempt at goal which was gathered by Senne Lammens. But the winger appeared to hurt himself in the process and had to be replaced by Alejandro Garnacho, who entered the fray against his former club for the first time since his £40million departure.

PIC

3. How may I assist you?

Watch out, Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, Bruno Fernandes is coming for your record. In setting up Cunha, the United captain registered his 18th assist of the season.

‌



Fernandes burst past ex-team-mate Garnacho on the right and played an inviting ball across the box for Cunha to smash home. The midfielder now only needs three more assists to break the all-time Premier League record. With five games left, who'd bet against him?

View 4 Images Bruno Fernandes has his eyes on the assist record (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

4. Toothless Chelsea

It's now 296 minutes and counting since Chelsea last scored a goal in the Premier League. After hitting four against Aston Villa in early March, the Blues haver been toothless in front of goal.

‌



Liam Delap got the nod in the absence of Joao Pedro here, and while he came close by hitting the bar in the second half, he couldn't end Chelsea's drought. Conceding goals is certainly a problem for Rosenior to address, but his side's failure to score them is arguably more concerning.

Who'll qualify for the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 4 Images Chelsea weren't able to end their drought (Image: Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



5. United go 10 clear

What a turnaround it's been from United. The Red Devils now have a huge buffer to sixth-placed Chelsea and are firmly on course to qualify for the Champions League.

Such a feat is likely to earn Carrick the job on a permanent basis, and although it wasn't always pretty in West London, his patched-up defence held on and got the job done.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi sends four-word message to Tottenham stars after Brighton heartbreak
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi sends four-word message to Tottenham stars after Brighton heartbreak

Tottenham were left feeling sick after conceding a 95th-minute equaliser at home to Brighton, having been on the cusp of jumping out of the Premier League relegation zone

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi was happy with how Tottenham played (Image: Hayters TV)

Defiant Roberto De Zerbi has reminded Tottenham's players that 'it's not finished yet' after they were left heartbroken against Brighton. Spurs were on course to move out of the relegation zone before conceding in the 95th minute on Saturday.

‌



Georginio Rutter capitalised on a mistake from Kevin Danso to snatch an equaliser after Xavi Simons had given Tottenham a precious lead in the second half. Brighton had fought back earlier in the game when Kaoru Mitoma cancelled out Pedro Porro's opening goal.

‌



It was, though, a much-improved performance from Spurs compared to last Sunday's drab 1-0 defeat at Sunderland, De Zerbi's first game in charge. The Italian was happy with his side's display and felt 'positive' despite the late goal.

‌



"If we are able to give our best, it's not finished yet," De Zerbi told Sky Sports post-match. "I said to (the players) be strong, to follow me again and again because I want to help them.

Premier League star in tears as agonising injury forces him off in Tottenham vs Brighton READ MORE :

"They can change the mentality because that is the most important part. Now it's too easy to think negative, but we have to be focused on this performance and work to find the condition to win again. I am positive because I know my players, I know their qualities. I know them like people and I believe in them."

‌



De Zerbi added: "I am positive but I am proud of my players. They played a fantastic game with character and spirit. We have to be stronger than this result, we have to move on and prepare the next game and try to win the game at Wolves. If you are strong like today, I think we can compete again."

Goalscorer Porro echoed his manager's sentiment, telling BBC Sport: "I think after the game we don't have time for the disappointment. For me and my team-mates, the best thing is keep pushing, keep going.

Will Tottenham avoid relegation? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Tottenham remain in the bottom three (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

"I think the team today was very good. I think first half was very good for us. The team pressed very well. I think the most important thing now is staying positive."

On Danso's error, Porro added: "I think Kevin had a great game today. This is the point now, we don't have time for mistakes. This is football, it happens. For me, today Kevin was instrumental on the pitch."

Sports.title: Man Utd left with Lisandro Martinez referee frustration after red card repeat missed
Sports.content:
Man Utd left with Lisandro Martinez referee frustration after red card repeat missed

Lisandro Martinez received a red card for violent conduct in the defeat to Leeds United, but a similar Premier League hair pull incident went unpunished

View 4 Images A new twist in the Lisandro Martinez red card saga has emerged with a similar Premier League incident taking place (Image: (Photo by Richard Martin-Roberts - CameraSport via Getty Images))

Manchester United's fury at Lisandro Martinez's dismissal appears to have intensified following a similar incident in the Premier League that didn't lead to a red card. The Argentine was sent off for violent conduct after tugging the hair of Dominic Calvert-Lewin during the loss to Leeds United.

‌



Just five days on from that incident, Dango Outtara carried out a similar act on Calvin Bassey during Fulham's visit to Brentford, yet referee Paul Tierney awarded only a foul. He was also the match official at Old Trafford earlier in the week, which further raises doubts about consistency in refereeing decisions.

‌



Given the minimal contact involved, it could have been easily overlooked by Tierney. Yet there was also no intervention from VAR, with Craig Pawson overseeing the system at Stockley Park.

‌



Man Utd dealt huge injury blow as Michael Carrick forced into rethink vs Chelsea READ MORE :

Earlier in the campaign, Everton defender Michael Keane was sent off for pulling the hair of Wolves' Tolu Arokodare.

While the minor contact from Outtara is arguably less severe than the pulls committed by Martinez and Keane, a standard has been established that any form of contact in that area warrants a dismissal.

View 4 Images Dango Outtara appeared to pull the hair of Calvin Bassey (Image: Premier League)

‌



As a consequence of the decision reached regarding Martinez, he will sit out three United league fixtures, with his suspension beginning for the match against Chelsea.

Harry Maguire is also banned for the trip to Stamford Bridge after being handed an additional one-game suspension for remarks directed at the fourth official following his red card against Bournemouth before the March international break.

View 4 Images Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was shown a straight red card against Leeds United (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

‌



To compound Michael Carrick's problems at centre-back, Leny Yoro did not make the journey to London, potentially through injury, which has also ruled him out of the Chelsea fixture.

Diogo Dalot has stepped in to replace him, with Noussair Mazraoui partnering Heaven in the heart of defence. Carrick has received a welcome fitness boost, however, with Kobbie Mainoo returning to the starting line-up after sitting out the Leeds fixture with a minor complaint.

View 4 Images Manchester United duo Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are both unavailable vs Chelsea due to suspension

Article continues below

There has also been a reshuffle in attack, with Bryan Mbeumo coming in for Amad on the right flank as Benjamin Sesko continues to lead the line.

It is a pivotal encounter for both sides in the battle for Champions League qualification, and a victory for the hosts over United would narrow the gap to just three points.

Sports.content:

Chelsea had to make an early substitution during their Premier League match against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge due to injury

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee's yellow card set on FIRE in Sidemen match at Wembley
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee's yellow card set on FIRE in Sidemen match at Wembley

Former Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg had his yellow card set on fire during the seventh Sidemen Charity Match by a YouTube star

View 3 Images YouTuber Max Fosh set a yellow card on fire during the Sidemen Charity Match (Image: Sidemen/YouTube)

Ex-Premier League referee Mark Clattenburg couldn't believe his eyes as his yellow card was set on fire by YouTuber Max Fosh in the Sidemen Charity Match. The pair do have history.

‌



The seventh annual Charity match hosted by trailblazing YouTube group the Sidemen raised over £6.2million for two chosen charities as 90,000 fans packed into Wembley Stadium. Supporters got value for money where goals were concerned, as the match itself finished 10-10 before KSI's YouTube Allstars prevailed 4-1 in a penalty shootout.

‌



But less than a minute into the second half, referee Clattenburg, who has taken charge of the match since 2022, was amazed to see Fosh burn his yellow card as he attempted to book the 31-year-old.

‌



Sidemen Charity Match ratings as YouTube Allstars win 20-goal thriller after penalty shootout READ MORE :

Fosh, famous for uploading online stunts and social experiments, including running for London mayor in 2021, first clashed with Clattenburg in 2023, when he was booked by the official and held up an Uno reverse card.

A year later, Fosh went into the book again but when Clattenburg produced the card this time around, he pulled out a miniature shredder and destroyed the card.

View 3 Images Fosh went into the book in the 46th minute (Image: Sidemen/YouTube)

‌



Fosh went one step further this time around. He appeared to purposely pick up a booking seconds after the break when dragging down an opponent and was destined to have his name taken by Clattenburg.

But as the referee raised his card, Fosh took it off him and after a few seconds it caught alight and disappeared. Clattenburg couldn't believe what he was seeing and put his hands to his face.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



This bit of trickery was overlooked and Fosh got away without any further punishment. He played the role of hero in the shootout too, and converted from 12 yards.

"I had six days. Had to come up with something. It worked about 50 per cent of the time when I practised it at home," Fosh said later on in the broadcast.

View 3 Images Clattenburg was taken aback by the act (Image: Sidemen/YouTube)

‌



Teams were allowed to challenge decisions made by Clattenburg this year and a moment of contention arose in the 27th minute, when TBJZL was penalised for a foul in the area. But it seemed he was fouled by JasonTheWeen before committing his own offence, and Clattenburg went to the big screen.

To the amazement of all those on the pitch, the penalty stood and SDMN FC goalkeeper XQC eventually saved it. This came before he gave the ball straight to Miniminter, who fired a shot between the shot-stopper's legs.

Miniminter, real name Simon Minter, bagged a hat-trick in the game, bringing his total to 14 goals in these charity matches, the current record.

Sports.content:
Man Utd dealt huge injury blow as Michael Carrick forced into rethink vs Chelsea

Manchester United travelled to Chelsea with only a single recognised centre-back following injuries to Leny Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, while Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are suspended

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has called on Ayden Heaven amid Manchester United's defensive crisis (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Noussair Mazraoui is set to partner Ayden Heaven at centre-back for Manchester United as part of a makeshift line-up against Chelsea. Michael Carrick has been forced to call on Mazraoui, a right-back by trade, and 19-year-old Heaven after Leny Yoro joined three of his fellow central defenders in missing the trip to Stamford Bridge.

‌



United were already with Matthijs de Ligt due to a long-term back injury before their crisis worsened this week. Firstly, Lisandro Martinez was shown a straight red card for violent conduct during Monday's limp 2-1 loss at home to Leeds.

‌



His suspension was upheld despite an appeal from United, and means that Martinez will be suspended for three matches. Then on Wednesday, it was confirmed that Harry Maguire would be also banned for the Chelsea game.

‌



Maguire's outburst towards the officials after being sent off during last month's 2-2 draw away to Bournemouth resulted in his one-match ban being extended to two. The centre-back also received a £30,000 fine.

Sports.title: Chelsea's CL hopes suffer another bitter blow in Man Utd defeat
Sports.content:
Chelsea's hopes of qualifying for next season's Champions League took another huge blow as they suffered a 1-0 defeat at home to Manchester United.

Matheus Cunha's goal on the stroke of half-time proved to be enough for Michael Carrick's side to solidify third place in the Premier League and leave Liam Rosenior's men further adrift of a return to Europe's elite competition.

Hundreds of Chelsea supporters protested against the clubs owners BlueCo prior to the game as they called for an end to the regime. And those inside the stadium voiced their dissatisfaction come the final whistle with boos that could be heard all around west London.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the game against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea and Strasbourg fans were involved in a peaceful protest against BlueCo's ownership

Team news: Enzo Fernandez returned to the midfield for Chelsea, but was not given the captain's armband following his comments on his future. Joao Pedro was absent from the squad, leaving Liam Delap to lead the line.

Noussair Mazraoui partnered Ayden Heaven at centre-back, while Kobbie Mainoo also returned from injury.

Chelsea dominated throughout the first-half, and can only be furious at themselves to not have been ahead at the break.

Willian Estevao clipped the outside of the post with a curling effort inside the first quarter of an hour, while the returning Enzo Fernandez spurned an even better opportunity as he shot wide from just outside the six-yard-box.

Image: Enzo Fernandez put a glorious opportunity wide before Man Utd took the lead

Up until their opener, United had managed an xG of just 0.03. However, with Wesley Fofana off the pitch after picking up a knock, they capitalised as Bruno Fernandes secured his 18th Premier League assist of the season by finding Cunha whose first time strike nestled into the top corner.

The Blues continued to look the more likely to score in the second period, with Liam Delap seeing his header cannon back off the crossbar just before the hour mark. A near identical chance then fell to Fofana, but he found the exact same result.

By hook or by crook, the unorthodox Manchester United back four that saw stellar performances from Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui at centre-back held on for a rare clean sheet to take all three points.

Image: Alejandro Garnacho struggled to make an impact against his former club

The home supporters loudly booed their team at the final whistle, both in disappointment of their lack of finishing touch and the fact they now find themselves 10 points behind United in the Premier League table.

They also remain four points behind fifth-placed Liverpool, having played a game more as their Champions League hopes slowly slip away.

Player ratings: Chelsea: Sanchez (6), Gusto (6), Fofana (5), Hato (6), Cucurella (5), Caicedo (5), Enzo Fernandez (6), Estevao (5), Palmer (6), Neto (6), Delap (6).



Subs: Garnacho (4), Acheampong (N/A), Chalobah (N/A), Lavia (N/A)



Man Utd: Lammens (6), Dalot (7), Mazraoui (7), Heaven (8), Shaw (7), Casemiro (6), Mainoo (6), Mbeumo (5), Fernandes (8), Cunha (7), Sesko (6).



Subs: Amad (N/A), Mount (N/A), Zirkzee (N/A)



Player of the Match: Ayden Heaven

Rosenior: We were the dominant team

Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior speaking with TNT Sports:

"Up until the box, we were very good. I can only say what I saw, I thought we were the dominant team from minute one until the end of the game.

"But to lose this game in the manner we did is extremely disappointing because we had many opportunities to win it.

"It's been a difficult spell. We're making key errors in key moments and we're not taking advantage of the chances we're creating.

"When you do that and you don't win games of football, it has to turnaround quickly.

"I'm delighted we have a game on Tuesday to get this out of our system and we have to go to Brighton and put things right.

"We created many chances today. It's not about the creation of the chances, but the taking of them.

"We hit the woodwork four times, so we're not far away."

On Champions League race:

"We just need to win the next game. We can't think about other teams, we have to focus on ourselves and we have to make sure we put things right."

Carrick: We're only looking forward in CL quest

Image: Liam Rosenior applauds the Chelsea fans after the defeat to Man Utd

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick speaking with TNT Sports:

"It was massive for us, a big win. To come here and keep a clean sheet like we did, and defend the way we did, I thought it was a magnificent performance.

"We don't want to look behind us, we want to keep improving and move forward. We're still not high enough, we want to be higher, but it was a big win and something the supporters can enjoy.

"It was a disappointment against Leeds, but to come here and respond like that, especially in a tough place, was really pleasing. Some games are about getting the result, and there's no shame in that.

On selecting his defence:

Image: Michael Carrick celebrating with makeshift centre-back Noussair Mazraoui at full-time

"There was a lot of work in the last couple of days preparing the team, especially with the new back four. Ayden [Heaven] and Nous [Mazraoui] coming in were incredible. At such a young age, Ayden isn't really playing centre-back in a back four, so a lot of credit goes to the coaching staff and the players for taking that on board."

Rosenior under severe pressure as Chelsea booed off again

Analysis from Sky Sports' Joe Shread:

That's six defeats in seven games for Chelsea. That's four defeats in a row in the Premier League - all without scoring.

Three home defeats in a row - the first time since 1993 they've managed that. And it's Chelsea's Champions League hopes in tatters.

Loud boos at full-time. The pressure on Liam Rosenior is red hot.

Chelsea's failure to score breaking all the wrong records Chelsea have lost, and failed to score, in each of their last four league games, only in November 1912 have the Blues ever endured a longer run in their league history (5 games).

Carrick's centre-back risk pays off

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

Many would've understandably questioned the decision to start Noussair Mazraoui at centre-back this evening. The Moroccan hasn't got much experience in that position, and he was partnering a youngster without much experience full stop in Ayden Heaven.

Pre-match, moving Luke Shaw central seemed to be the most obvious option. Perhaps Manuel Ugarte too after he slotted in during the defeat to Leeds.

Instead, it was Mazraoui. The ultimate utility man. And it paid off too. He looked calm on the ball and didn't get too exploited aerially, even if there were one or two moments.

He has played all across the defence, slotted into the holding midfield role. He's even tried out as a number 10. But of all his makeshift performances, this was by far his best yet.

Sports.title: Rosenior admits he doesn't know consequences of no CL football
Sports.content:
Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior has admitted he doesn't know what consequences the Blues will face if they fail to qualify for the Champions League.

Rosenior's side lost yet more ground in the race for the top five as they suffered a 1-0 defeat at home to Manchester United.

The result leaves Chelsea 10 points behind the Red Devils in the table, and four behind fifth-placed Liverpool ahead of their Merseyside derby with Everton.

Prior to the game, Cole Palmer claimed to have no plans to leave Stamford Bridge and suggested that qualifying for Europe's elite competition "is a good position to sign players that we need."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liam Rosenior said he wasn't surprised by rumours linking Cole Palmer away from Chelsea earlier in the season

However, failure to be in the Champions League this season could not only impact the incomings next summer, but also the outgoings. And Rosenior admitted he didn't know how missing out on the competition will change the direction of plans moving forward.

"The honest answer is I don't know," Rosenior said in his post-match press conference.

"The honest answer is we're still fighting and we will address that situation at the end of the season, whatever the situation is."

What Palmer said about Champions League qualifcation

Palmer was asked about his future in west London during an interview with The Guardian, where he played down suggestions that he could look to leave the club.

However, he also stressed the importance of needing to qualify for the Champions League in order to secure the players needed to improve the team and help them achieve their long-term goals.

"I've got no plans to move from Chelsea. We've still got a lot to play for," he said.

Image: Cole Palmer has said that Chelsea qualifying for the Champions League will put them in a good spot

"We've got the FA Cup semi-final [against Leeds] and if we finish in a Champions League spot it puts us in a good position to sign players that we need.

"We spoke to the owners and they're sure of the players that are gonna do it. Reece won't sign a six-year contract if he's not spoken to the owners and the directors.

"Me and Reece [James] spoke a lot. About things we need, players we need to sign and how things need to be. He wouldn't sign a new contract if he didn't know what was going on.

"The manager is good and when he has a proper pre-season and gets his ideas across properly and the way he wants to play he's a top coach."

Rosenior says Champions League 'mountain' not 'insurmountable'

With just five Premier League games left to go, Chelsea will be relying on the likes of Liverpool and Aston Villa slipping up in order to climb back into the Champions League places.

However, with pressure from the likes of Brentford, Bournemouth, Brighton and Everton behind them, there's every chance the Blues could slip further down the table if they don't turn their form around.

The Blues have six of their last seven games in the Premier League, including their last four. They have also failed to score in those last four games, their worst run since 1912.

However, Rosenior believes there is still a chance they can qualify for Europe's elite competition.

"It gives us a mountain to climb," he added.

"It's not insurmountable. We have to go into Brighton with an idea that we have to win that game and kick-start the rest of our season."

Sports.title: Bromley promoted to League One for first time in their history
Sports.content:
Bromley have been promoted to League One for the first time in their history with two games of the season to spare.

The Ravens were made to wait to achieve the feat after losing to MK Dons and drawing with Cambridge over the past week.

But Notts County's defeat to Barnet on Saturday means the League Two leaders can no longer be caught in the automatic promotion places.

Founded in 1892, the Ravens took 132 years to reach the EFL, but in just their second season they have reached the third tier.
